title: Immutable audit policies, ILM and egress controls review with Seraphic Finance
next_steps: Redwood to share immutable-audit design doc and S3 export config (Jordan) — target 2026-08-24
Seraphic to provide retention policy requirements and legal hold scenarios (Aisha) — target 2026-08-26
Schedule a technical pilot for streaming audit events to Seraphic's Kafka cluster (Elena + Diego) — proposed week of 2026-08-31
action_items: Jordan: send design doc + sample export schema by 2026-08-24
Elena: prepare demo script for Kafka/HTTPS streaming and include failure/retry behavior by 2026-08-28
Diego: provide a list of PKI/KMS policies and current HSM vendor details by 2026-08-26
summary: Conversation focused on what Redwood captures for admin/audit events, immutable retention patterns (ILM/legal hold), export options (S3, Kafka, webhook), and encryption/KMS integration for Seraphic's EU data residency and finance compliance needs.
topics: events captured: admin, api-key, role changes, model deploys, token ops
immutable retention / time-based ILM and legal hold
export sinks: S3 (AES256 + SSE-KMS), Kafka, HTTPS/webhook, FTP (rare)
KMS integration: bring-your-own-key (BYOK), HSM, key rotation
RBAC/SSO audit trails: SAML/SCIM provisioning events
data residency and cross-region egress controls
transcript:
Header: 2026-08-19 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Elena (SE), Maya (CSM); Marcus (CTO), Aisha (Head of Compliance), Diego (Platform Eng)

[00:00] Jordan Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:06] Marcus Leung: Marcus here.
[00:08] Aisha Rahman: Aisha on my side.
[00:10] Diego Morales: Diego present.
[00:12] Jordan Patel: great; so main agenda — audit capture, retention/immutability, and how you can pull/export logs for long-term storage and legal hold. elena will walk through the export patterns.
[00:25] Elena Cho: hey all. quick note, i'll try to show the streaming and S3 flows. please interrupt with specifics, we can dive deeper.
[00:35] Aisha Rahman: high level — Seraphic needs immutable admin logs for 7 years for reconciliations. can you confirm what you capture and whether that can be marked immutable?
[00:45] Elena Cho: yes, so out of the box we capture auth events (login/sso failures), token creation and revocation, api key lifecycle, role grants/revokes, admin UI actions, CLI/SDK calls that hit management plane, model deploys, model version rollbacks, and policy changes. note: some infra-level telemetry like node-heartbeats are not in the audit log, those are metrics only.
[01:10] Marcus Leung: when you say "model deploys" — is that full payload or just metadata? we can't store model blobs.
[01:18] Elena Cho: just metadata — model id, version, operator, timestamp, git sha reference if available, size estimate. we don't capture weights or model files.
[01:28] Jordan Patel: to clarify, PII is not captured by default in audit fields — user identifiers are obfuscated to UIDs, and we provide a redaction config if you'd prefer stricter removal.
[01:40] Aisha Rahman: redaction is important. also need chain-of-custody for any modifications to the logs — can Redwood prevent deletion or provide append-only storage?
[01:50] Elena Cho: there are two patterns. 1) platform-side immutability using Write-Once-Read-Many (WORM) export to S3 with object lock enabled. 2) export to your Kafka with retention and ACLs enforced by your cluster; combined with signed manifests we can show append-only evidence.
[02:15] Diego Morales: for S3 WORM — do you support object lock with a legal hold API so we can programmatically place holds?
[02:22] Jordan Patel: short answer yes, via our export pipeline you can push objects to your S3 bucket with object lock enabled and we set the retention via metadata. legal hold can be toggled by you. we'll include example IAM policy and a CloudFormation snippet.
[02:35] Elena Cho: also note we sign each export manifest with a service-side key so you get tamper-evident logs; that signature is verifiable.
[02:42] Aisha Rahman: about encryption — we are required to use our KMS (on-prem HSM) for key custody. do you support BYOK / external KMS?
[02:51] Elena Cho: yes. Redwood supports using your KMS via a key-wrapping flow. for hosted customers we integrate with AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure Key Vault, and for private deployments we support on-prem HSMs and HSM-backed KMS. key rotation is supported; we provide rewrap operations for archives.
[03:12] Marcus Leung: what's the latency impact on exports? we need near-real-time for fraud ops (sub-2s not required, but sub-30s preferred).
[03:20] Elena Cho: for streaming to Kafka/HTTPS we can push events within ~3–10s under normal load. S3 batch exports are typically hourly by default but can be configured to, say, 5m windows if you accept higher cost.
[03:34] Diego Morales: do you capture RBAC changes from SSO/SAML provisioning — like SCIM user create/deactivate events?
[03:40] Jordan Patel: yes, SCIM events, SAML assertion failures, and IdP-initiated sessions are logged. we also capture provisioning diffs so you can reconcile assigned groups/roles.
[03:52] Aisha Rahman: for audit schema, can you provide a sample? we need to map to our SIEM fields.
[03:58] Elena Cho: i'll attach a JSON schema post-call; quick preview: event_type, actor_id (pseudonymized), target_id, action, timestamp, request_id, ip, region, request_payload_summary, response_code, signature, export_manifest_id.
[04:18] Marcus Leung: signature and manifest id — good. does signature use a customer key at rest or Redwood key?
[04:25] Elena Cho: signatures on exports are Redwood-signed by default, but for enterprise we support HSM-signing with your key via BYOK/HSM integration — that gives you full chain control.
[04:36] Aisha Rahman: data residency — our EU customers' logs must stay in eu-central only. can exports be region pinned?
[04:44] Jordan Patel: yes, for Private and Dedicated we can pin the control plane and export sinks to eu-central. for Hosted we provide region-scoped exports to customer buckets in the same region. cross-region replication is opt-in and off by default.
[04:58] Diego Morales: about retention — we will have multiple classes: 90 days hot, 2 years warm, 7 years cold immutable. what's best practice?
[05:07] Elena Cho: typical pattern: streaming into Kafka for hot (retention short), S3 with lifecycle rules for warm-to-cold, and Glacier/Archive tier for 7-year cold. for immutability use S3 Object Lock governance or compliance mode plus manifests and signed timelines. ILM policies can be kept in your infra repo.
[05:32] Aisha Rahman: how do you handle legal holds that override lifecycle?
[05:37] Jordan Patel: legal hold flags on manifests prevent lifecycle transitions. when legal hold is set we keep object lock until release. We'll show the API you call that toggles a hold.
[05:50] Marcus Leung: is there an export that includes full audit trail plus the raw request payload for forensics? sometimes we need the prompt and response for an incident.
[05:59] Elena Cho: we do capture request/response summaries by default and you can opt-in to full payload export, but that requires additional review because it can contain PII and model outputs. for finance we'll recommend scrubbing or encrypted vault storage. If you opt in we can stream to a separate encrypted bucket with stricter KMS controls.
[06:22] Aisha Rahman: any built-in retention reporting or attestation logs?
[06:28] Elena Cho: yes, Console has per-export audit status, manifest hashes, and an evidence pack (zip) that includes manifests, signatures, and a retention timeline. That evidence pack is what auditors typically request.
[06:40] Diego Morales: about incident replay — can we replay event sequences into a sandbox?
[06:45] Jordan Patel: yes, we provide a replay utility that rehydrates events into a dedicated sandbox environment, minus secrets. Replay configs are stored in your exports area and we scrub credentials automatically.
[06:57] Aisha Rahman: SSO: do you log the raw SAML assertion?
[07:02] Elena Cho: we log SAML assertion metadata and assertion id, but not the full assertion by default — though for incident response we can provide a secure export of the full assertion under strict controls.
[07:15] Marcus Leung: competitor question — how does this compare to pushing everything into Splunk?
[07:20] Jordan Patel: similar in terms of collection, but our exports are tailored to the inference control plane (model events, token lifecycle) and we provide turnkey manifests/schemas to simplify SIEM mapping. if you want, we can demo Splunk HEC forwarding but most customers prefer Kafka/S3 then ingest into Splunk.
[07:38] Diego Morales: about throughput — can you sustain 5k events/sec during peak testing?
[07:44] Elena Cho: our hosted export pipeline can burst; for sustained high throughput we recommend Dedicated with reserved export workers or using our streaming endpoint directly to your Kafka — that's the lowest-latency path.
[07:58] Aisha Rahman: okay next — proof of immutability: auditors want to see tamper evidence and chain of custody. what do you hand them?
[08:08] Elena Cho: evidence pack: signed manifests, object lock metadata, export delivery receipts, and a timeline showing when legal holds were applied/removed. We can also provide attestations signed by our security team.
[08:22] Jordan Patel: i'll include a sample evidence pack in the follow up.
[08:26] Marcus Leung: one more on key rotation — if we rotate keys, can we still decrypt old archives?
[08:33] Elena Cho: yes, we support key rewrap: archives are wrapped with a data key encrypted under your KMS key; when you rotate we rewrap the data key under the new KMS key so old archives remain accessible if you allow it.
[08:48] Diego Morales: any gotchas with cross-account S3? permissions get messy.
[08:52] Jordan Patel: we'll provide exact IAM policies and an example bucket policy that locks down puts to only our export role, and separate read roles for your auditors.
[08:59] Aisha Rahman: what about monitoring of exports? alerts on failed deliveries?
[09:03] Elena Cho: yes, Console has delivery metrics and alert hooks; failed deliveries go into a retry queue and generate incidents. we can stream delivery failures to your pager or to a webhook.
[09:16] Marcus Leung: ok, that's helpful. any privacy or PII minimization features we should know?
[09:21] Jordan Patel: redaction templates, configurable hashing/pseudonymization, and field-level encryption for sensitive fields. also you can route sensitive payloads to a stricter bucket.
[09:33] Aisha Rahman: last question — can we enforce RBAC so only compliance team can see full payloads?
[09:38] Elena Cho: yes, RBAC at the route/model/export level. We have attribute-based controls so you can grant the compliance role the ability to request unredacted exports; actions are logged and require extra approval in the console.
[09:54] Diego Morales: cool. next step for us is pilot. Diego and El will set up Kafka topic details and a test namespace.
[10:02] Jordan Patel: recap — Jordan shares design docs and evidence pack sample; Elena sets up pilot plan; Aisha provides retention/legal hold scenarios. We'll reconvene after pilot readiness.
[10:15] Aisha Rahman: thanks all, that covers my concerns for now.
[10:18] Marcus Leung: thanks.
[10:20] Jordan Patel: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with artifacts. bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hears: 'H S M' sometimes transcribed as 'HSM' or 'H S M', 'SCIM' sometimes spoken as 'skim', 'KV cache' heard as 'kay vee cache'. Speakers occasionally overlap; timestamps approximate every ~30–90s.
